quest.title: Reunion Beneath the Moonlight
quest.description: The secrets of this land are like an ancient song that lingers in your heart and cannot be easily dismissed... What song shall Nod-Krai play for you this night...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1650, Mora x72975, Hero's Wit x7, Mystic Enhancement Ore x13

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act I
chapter.title: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves

talks.objective: Return to The Flagship to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zzz... Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nod-Krai... A land steeped in ancient stories... and the "first" place I set foot in Teyvat...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Fatui... they seem to be conducting some kind of research on the Ancient Moon's Remnants... and now they're after the Frostmoon Scions' sacred Moon Marrow...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (And then there's The Damselette... Kuutar, the moonborn...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why did she leave the Frostmoon Scions in the first place? And why did she then abandon the Fatui?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lauma mentioned "family"...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether}... What happened to our spaceship back then? Why did we land in Teyvat?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ugh... My head's spinning... I won't be able to sleep like this...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'll try not to dwell on it. Just need to try to get some sleep...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *snore*... Hehe... Just one more... helping...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ha... I envy Paimon sometimes... She really can fall asleep anywhere...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ugh, no use forcing it... Maybe a walk will clear my head...)

dialogues.speaker: Message
dialogues.text: "Paimon, I'm heading out for a bit. If you wake up and I'm still gone, don't panic... I'll be back soon."

talks.objective: Take a walk under the moonlight

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (And Varka just happened to be away... Could it somehow be related to the Abyss...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Come to think of it... It feels like there's something different about the Abyssal phenomenon here... the one they call the "Wild Hunt"...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? Didn't realize I'd walked this far already...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Guess I should head back soon... If I'm gone too long, Paimon will start to worry...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait, is that... singing?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: These flowers... I remember... When you first appeared, there were flowers like this all around you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's heading towards the source of the singing... Might as well follow it and see what's going on...)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Been slacking off on your combat training? Or has no one been around to keep you in shape?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No... I... just wanted to let you win.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Been too busy practicing your excuses instead, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wonder when the last time we bickered like this was... Miss those days, I really do.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That girl... She looks just like the Frostmoon Scions' statues... Surely that's not...!)
Who goes there?
How did you get in here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I am but a passing traveler... I followed your song here. I'm very sorry if I've intruded...
The kuuhenki... She brought you here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What do I do now...? Did I just wander into her private abode? Should I... leave?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... I have questions I really want to ask her...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May I ask... Are you the one they call "Kuutar"? And... the Harbinger that the Fatui refer to as "The Damselette"?
...The Fatui?
Are you here at their behest?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What's going on? These flowers, did they just... turn red? And that... sudden sense of impending danger!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please, don't get me wrong! I have no intention of doing anything for the Fatui!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I just wanted to ask you about Nod-Krai... and the moons.
...The moons?
...Do not believe in what you can see. What truly matters is what you cannot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That feeling of danger has gone. Guess she no longer sees me as a threat... for now, at least. But...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Isn't she going to answer? She doesn't seem willing to speak...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's give that another try...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #...Listen, I'm {NICKNAME}. I'm on a journey through the nations of Teyvat.
#Hello, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Is that it?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Doesn't she know how a conversation's meant to work? Or does she just not care?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me your name?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So it is her...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Kuutar, The Damselette, the Moon Goddess... Pick whichever takes your fancy.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I do not know my own name.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...We're all given our name by someone else... but according to Lauma, she was born in Teyvat alone... So that must be why...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then... Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hm?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...I'd like to ask about the Fatui, but after the way she reacted last time I mentioned them... maybe not.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This kuuhenki, this Luonnotar... Did you bring her into being?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Come here, little one...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mmm... The trace of a blessing, but not one of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So maybe it's just like Lauma said... a blessing from long, long ago...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: People always assume I can do many things, assume I have done many things... but I haven't...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: All I ever wanted was to...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She's drifting off again...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So many mysteries remain unsolved, but we're not getting anywhere like this. Maybe this just isn't the right moment...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's about time I got going. I'm very sorry for disturbing you today...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Time to head back...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Luonnotar... Does it want to come with me?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina... That kuuhenki...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh... you're leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Not willing to let it go...? It seems she likes this Luonnotar a lot...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Go then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Take care... The moon can be treacherous.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? What does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Never mind. I'll ask her next time I get a chance to see her...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry to—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh? There's no one here. But didn't they just say Lauma came this way a few minutes ago?

dialogues.speaker: Black Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No one except for a... cat, watching over the front desk...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse... meow? Are we supposed to check in here?

dialogues.speaker: Black Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No idea what that means... Is this Lauma's personal receptionist, or something? Pretty sure she'd be the only person who could actually understand it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It's heading into that room...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But... Why not?
Like I told you already, that's just— Hmm? Another client?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah! So you were in this room the whole time...
Something I can do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...
Oh? You're acquainted, then?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. They visited Hiisi Island yesterday — we had dinner together.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Allow me to introduce you. {NICKNAME}, Paimon... This is Nefer, boss of the Curatorium of Secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Pleasure to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They are travelers who arrived in Nod-Krai just yesterday. Greeted by the birds and beasts of this land, they are kind-hearted souls who walk in the moonlight's glow...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Hmm? Ha, interesting...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, I, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lauma, but you need not have introduced them. They are great heroes, renowned throughout the nations beyond our borders.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Oh, really...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Do not forget, I deal in information. Just because most people in Nod-Krai pay scant attention to foreign affairs, that does not mean the same goes for the Curatorium of Secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: They're the heroes everyone was talking about before — the ones who saved Natlan during the Abyss crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Help... I've never felt this uncomfortable being praised before... How am I supposed to explain what happened last night now?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I see... We Frostmoon Scions seldom leave our domain, so I had not heard of your heroic deeds. Please, forgive my ignorance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's no big deal, we were hoping to keep a low profile anyway. If we had to list all of our titles and good deeds, we'd be talking till sundown, and then some!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong? Still not feeling great?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, what brings you both to the Curatorium today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ohhh, so basically, we were just eating when we overheard people talking about how the Frostmoon Scions' relic had been stolen... and then {M#he}{F#she} dragged Paimon over here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Mm... I see.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Ah, I see! So you came over here because you were worried about Lauma? A combination truly befitting of great heroes — strong at arms and pure of heart.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I can't take this much longer...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In that case, Lauma, I've got a suggestion.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Why not ask these battle-hardened heroes to take the commission for you? Honestly, it's a little beyond the means of such a modest establishment as ours.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Your "modest establishment," unable to handle a commission? You just don't want to take it, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're right — I do not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of commission is this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely it's not... to recover your stolen relic?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes, that is it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Recovering the relic is both my duty as a Moonchanter and a step toward fulfilling the promise I made {NICKNAME} — to help uncover the truth of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But Nefer has already declined our commission multiple times.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And yet, just as it always has, the moon will continue to illuminate the sky above the Curatorium.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Come night or day, may the Moon Goddess keep you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Enough of that.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #(So... according to {M#him}{F#her}, {M#he}{F#she} never came into contact with the relic... so {M#he}{F#she} suspects {M#his sister}{F#her brother} may have taken it.)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Mm... I understand.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm truly sorry...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...The Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber has remained hidden from the world for generations. But the reason outsiders are forbidden entry is not only to prevent theft.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Within the chamber lie ancient trials, challenges designed to test the worthiness of those who enter. To intrude without rightful cause is a most perilous act indeed.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #So please, don't be too hard on yourself, {NICKNAME}. The fact that you made it through those trials proves your right to stand before the relic.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: To put it simply... the Moon Marrow itself has deemed you worthy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You're not angry with me?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No. Your honesty tells me everything — you never sought to take the Moon Marrow for yourself.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: As for what happened at the end... I suspect the chamber's protection mechanism may have been activated. Among those who entered the final chamber, there was either someone with impure intent, or else... an Abyssal presence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Abyss?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Perhaps that's why, then. Either way, the Moon Marrow was taken...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...And I believe you, so the problem remains the same. I need to recover our relic.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: See? Didn't I tell you it would all work out in the end?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #But before everyone starts celebrating, forgive me for asking just one more thing... Are you absolutely sure your {M#sister}{F#brother} took the relic?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean? Weren't they the only ones inside at the time?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Who knows? Think about it — after your {M#sister}{F#brother} broke the seal with Abyssal power, what was to stop someone else from following you in there?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm... In theory, nothing.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And as it just so happens, I received a tip-off from one of my sources earlier this morning...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Word is, today of all days, the Fatui suddenly called off their search for the relic.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, either they woke up this morning and suddenly decided they'd lost all interest, or...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They already have it.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(But... no... {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} couldn't possibly be working with the Fatui...)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Are you wondering if your {M#sister}{F#brother} might be in cahoots with the Fatui?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Which is why I asked: Are you absolutely sure your {M#sister}{F#brother} took the relic?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: #Or to put it another way... Do you really know your {M#sister}{F#brother}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(She's right... The truth is, I really don't know what {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} is trying to do here...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: In other words... it's highly likely that the Fatui already have the Moon Marrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So basically, all we need to do is find our way into that Fatui research facility, and we should be able to get to the bottom of this, right?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Congratulations, you've found your answer! Looks like the Curatorium won't need to lift a finger this time.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, Lauma, there we are... On behalf of our longstanding cooperation, and the great hero by your side, I'll waive your consultation fee — but just this once.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...You're really not planning on helping us?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I think I've helped more than enough already.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If we're to stand any chance of infiltrating that facility, we'll need the help of a specialist.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: *sigh* Just so you don't get the wrong idea, let me make myself crystal clear...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The Curatorium of Secrets has always striven to abide by a policy of strict neutrality. We do not take sides with any faction in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I cannot help the leader of the Frostmoon Scions sneak into a Fatui facility. That would make me their enemy.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: When one of their Harbingers asked me to help them infiltrate your territory, I gave them the same answer — "No."

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Alright, I understand.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But I do have one final request... I promise it's my last.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...It had better be.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No matter who it is, I want you to help us persuade the next person who walks through that door to join us.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: (What is she up to...?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You're that desperate for help? What if it's a member of the Fatui?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: It doesn't matter. You're welcome to tell them everything, even about our plans to infiltrate the Experimental Design Bureau.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: All I'm asking is for you to say one thing, just one thing to help persuade them. If you do that, I promise I won't ask you for anything else.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Made up your mind?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Fine, fine. I'll play along with your little game.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Besides, as long as I'm not personally involved, no one can accuse us of taking sides...
Boss, I'm back!
You won't believe the luck I've been having today! Remember you sent me to find that runaway cat, yeah? And you said I'd only be back after dark?
Well, guess what? Right after I left the house, this big ibis flew over, and the missing cat was right in its claws! And once it got close, it loosened its grip, and—
...Ahh! Boss, you're... meeting clients? I'm so sorry, I'll... get out of your way!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That ibis... must've been sent by Lauma...)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Jahoda, dear, come here.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh? Me...? Uh... Is something the matter? Oh, uh... Hi there...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: My dear Jahoda, I have a... request.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Yikes! Why does the boss sound so... scary? Did I do something wrong?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Would you be so kind as to accompany these three delightful clients of ours and help them infiltrate the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (What is going on here!? Boss usually just says things like "Hey, go do this," or "You, go take care of that." Why is she being so... scarily polite?)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (And... Wait a sec, the Fatui's research facility!? That's basically a death sentence!)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Made your mind up yet, my dear?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Uhhh... I... I...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (What is up with Boss today? Am I supposed to say yes to this!? Or... or maybe it's because the mission's too risky, so she's actually looking out for me...?)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Why is everyone looking at me like that!? Is this... some kind of test? I—I can't let Boss down... Can I?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Have you... made up... your mind?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Ahhh! I... Uh, umm... Th—That's... Sure, why not?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? You really don't mind helping us?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh? Oh, umm... Yes... I—I mean, no! Of course I... I mean, I... I guess I do...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks so much! We owe ya big time!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: On behalf of the Frostmoon Scions, too — thank you, Jahoda, for your help.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (What the...!? Seriously, what just happened?)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Why does the boss look so fed up? Oh no, was I supposed to turn them down...?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: (Ha... All that mentoring, time spent teaching her how to deal with different factions... in one ear and out the other...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Nefer...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You got what you wanted. You promised that was it.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I know this goes against your principles. I won't forget the favor.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ha... Trying to get me to change my mind now?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Of course not. I just wanted to say thank you.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: So... Thank you.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Jahoda, we'll leave the planning to you. Let's discuss the details elsewhere.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh? O—Okay...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (What have I got myself into...?)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh — by the way, Jahoda, before you go...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Uh... What is it, boss?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...You're fired.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Effective immediately. As in, this exact moment.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The Curatorium will take you back, of course — but only once you've completed this commission for our three clients.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: ...What!?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Is there some issue? Well, here's the upside — without me taking a cut from your commission, you'll earn more.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: ...Seriously, can someone explain what is going on here!?

choices.text: ...Can indeed wield the power of the Abyss.
There's something I need to get off my chest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's over!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Nicely done. Flawless execution.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Couldn't have pulled it off without your backup. Not too shabby at all.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: As for what you were saying... Yes, I should've come to see you earlier. Or at the very least...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Spent more time with me, going on adventures like this?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Instead of just running off and expecting you to follow my trail...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... That's not an official apology, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: That goes without saying.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: C'mon. Time to claim the treasure we came for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So The Damselette has been here on Hiisi Island all along... But if it wasn't for the Luonnotar, I would've never even found the way in.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She didn't seem all that concerned about the world outside. Why do the Fatui want her back so badly?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("The moon can be treacherous"... What's that supposed to mean...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, is that—!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #...{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(...Why is {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} here?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#She's}{F#He's} alone... Could {M#she}{F#he} be planning something?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #...{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #...{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}, it's you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#She}{F#He} doesn't seem that surprised to see me. Did {M#she}{F#he} already know I was in Nod-Krai?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are you here on Hiisi Island?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: If I told you I was here in search of the Frostmoon Scions' sacred relic... What would you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(So {M#Lumine's}{F#Aether's} looking for the Moon Marrow too? But surely {M#she}{F#he} can't be working with the Fatui... so what is {M#she}{F#he} after?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you also here to uncover the truth about our past?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: What happened to us in the past, how we came to Teyvat, why our spaceship crashed here... There are things I want to know too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(So even {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} doesn't know?)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: But I'm not about to sit around waiting for another two months to find out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait...!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Wait? But I still have unfinished business.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's... the way to the statue of "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar"...!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Surely {M#Lumine's}{F#Aether's} not here to...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hold on a second!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's the Frostmoon Scions' sacred relic. We can't just...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: ...Use it to get to the bottom of all this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should at least get their permission...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: You barely even know her, yet already you hold that "Moonchanter" in such high trust?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: She told you that the seal can only be broken on Moon-Prayer Night, when the flow of kuuvahki is at its peak, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You heard all that?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Watch this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Get it now? She's been stalling for time.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: As long as the statue's base is imbued with sufficient power, the secret chamber can be opened at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether} used Abyssal power, not kuuvahki... Yet {M#she's}{F#he's} broken the seal all the same.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Did the Abyssal power override the seal's kuuvahki?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Or has {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} been telling the whole truth, and nothing but...? Maybe Lauma's just afraid of breaking with tradition?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Who should I trust...?)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Is it such a sin when I don't put all my cards on the table for you, but not when someone else is doing it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...It's not like that.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}, you've got it all wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This whole time, I've wanted to ask you — what happened to make you like this? I admit, I've been having trouble accepting it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But after all this time apart, I've finally come to terms with who you are... willful side and all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I trust you, I still do. Through all the worlds we've traveled, you've always been there by my side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If there are things you can't explain yet... I can wait, while the journey goes on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll wait, as long as it takes... until the day you're ready to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Probably shouldn't have said all that... Must've sounded super sentimental.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But the truth is, I've bottled that up for way too long already...)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: I'm not looking to borrow the Moon Marrow simply because of our past.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: It holds answers... about the very origins of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: I've always believed that if you want the truth, you have to see the whole story for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #I'm not asking you to trust me, {M#Aether}{F#Lumine}. Just... don't try and stop me.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: If this choice weighs on your heart, then let me go in alone. Forget this meeting ever took place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bit late for that now...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: But maybe this is the chance I've been waiting for all along.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Even if it fades with the morning light...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I... want to go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: You sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Then let's go...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: It's been ages since we went on an adventure together. I can't wait.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Really...?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #You think I'd lie to my {M#big bro}{F#little sis}?

talks.objective: Enter the sanctum of the Frostmoon Scions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon would never have guessed Lauma had all that bottled up inside...

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Hey! Watch your step!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaah! Wh—What's wrong? You scared Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Whew... You scared me there, too. Almost stepped right into one of my traps...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A trap? Why would you leave a trap somewhere like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Well, it's not like this is a main path... and besides, we Frostmoon Scions would recognize it instantly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you trying to catch?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Hmm... Alright. You don't seem like you're with the Fatui, so I guess there's no harm telling you.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Lauma asked me to set up these traps to keep the Fatui at bay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh... Come to think of it, their three-day ultimatum is almost up now...

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Yes... Hopefully, they'll back off when they realize we won't go down without a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you've done a lot for the Frostmoon Scions too, just like Lauma...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Vilemina?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Ah! It's nothing, I... I was just wondering... if any of this is really worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Our people... so many are stubborn, stuck in their ways... clinging to a "truth" they refuse to even question.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Do they... really deserve everything Lauma's doing for them?

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: Well, yes, but even so...

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: No... I—I shouldn't be saying this. Just... forget it, okay? Bye!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: (Why did I say all that... or really... why am I still doing any of this...)

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: (*sigh*... Either way, this will be my final night with the Frostmoon Scions...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, she sure took off fast... So, are we heading back to The Flagship for a break, or what?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's still somewhere I wanted to go...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're not thinking of visiting that "Damselette" up in cloud cuckoo land, are you...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Given who she is, pushing her won't get us anywhere. Hmm... Hey, why don't we...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Let's bring her something tasty!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If she doesn't wanna talk, we'll have to win her over with food!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You really think it'll be that easy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, no harm in trying! At the very least, it shows we're trying to be friendly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, let's see... How about Ineffa's "9.12/10" Berries and Fried Meat, the Frostmoon Scions' boon of the day, and one of your signature dishes — your choice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should be a good mix of meat and veggies... there's bound to be something she likes!

choices.text: But if she just refuses to talk again...

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: Afraid... Huh. I suppose... maybe you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}, do you understand how kuuvahki works? How it exacts force through push and pull?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Okay, I'll leave it to you then.

choices.text: What do I need to do?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Let's see... How about this — I'll temporarily neutralize the kuuvahki on the cliff face and move the platform into the center.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Once it's in place, you'll need to utilize the repelling force of kuuvahki to reach the other side.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Gotcha.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Okay, I'll leave it to you then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, food's packed and ready. This is the place, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does it feel like we're going to visit a patient... Ugh, no, no, take this seriously, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: A wide, open space... must be in for a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Was that it? What a letdown...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(That look on {M#Lumine's}{F#Aether's} face... It's so... unlike {M#her}{F#him}.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Was {M#she}{F#he} scarred by {M#her}{F#his} experiences while we were apart? Each day a mark in {M#her}{F#his} flesh, until {M#she}{F#he} ended up like this...)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Why are you looking at me like that? Those enemies were weak, were they not?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: M—Maybe it's because the trial's only just begun...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Actually, I've got an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Why don't we have ourselves a little friendly competition?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Let's see if your journey has made you rusty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I won't lose to you, {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: No sign of any monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Feels like a ritual site... but something's missing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's ahead, inside that thing that looks like a mirror. I can feel it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But... maybe it's sealed within?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Can you open it using kuuvahki?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Apparently not.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you think it might have something to do with the Frostmoon Scions' bloodline?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Ha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: If this is about strength of blood, what could possibly stop us?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Let me give it a try. Why don't you check around for other clues?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Found it. This should do the trick.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As expected, the stone pillars seem to resonate with it!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: They're in your hands, then.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Looks like the final trial is just up ahead. Ready for battle?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When have I ever not been?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Going on an adventure with you, side by side... It's been so exciting. But at the same time, it just feels... surreal, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Maybe because it's been so long.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: You know, this is only the second time we've fought together since the day we both woke up in Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe that's it...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}, let the light of our blades come together once more, just like they did in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: This is a night of miracles, an adventure that belongs to us. Let's not weigh it down with worries and regrets.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: This is our adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Fine, you win.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't feel like you really wanted it anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Going all out in a place like this? Sounds like overkill to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wonder when the last time we bickered like this was... Miss those days, I really do.)

talks.objective: Enter the secret space where the relic is stored

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So this is the Moon Marrow... the treasure we've been after.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #Alright... Go get it for me, {M#Aether}{F#Lumine}. It belongs to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Huh? What's up with {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}? {M#She's}{F#He's} talking like a complete stranger again...)

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #What's wrong, {M#Aether}{F#Lumine}? After everything we've just been through, you still don't trust me?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Don't you want to know the truth too, just like I do?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Rest assured — I'll share the truth with you afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Now, go bring it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on? Where did this fog come from?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? What is this place?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That presence... it's the Abyss!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is that... the Wild Hunt? Did it show up when we entered this domain?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #Huh? What are you doing here, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're... Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Yes, we ran into each other at The Flagship this afternoon. I'm honored you still remember.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Is {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}... gone...?)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Are you looking for something here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Uh... Not sure I wanna admit that I just broke into the Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber in search of their sacred relic...)

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And you just happened to end up... surrounded by the Wild Hunt?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Sorry, I did not intend to come off as pointing fingers. Indeed, perhaps our courses of action do not differ so greatly.

choices.text: You're out for a walk too?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Not exactly. We Lightkeepers are accustomed to patrolling at night — a long-held tradition, you understand. I was just passing by when I noticed that the Wild Hunt had struck, so I simply did what I am duty-bound to do.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: As a matter of fact, I just saw someone leaving in quite the hurry. Was that your companion?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(...! {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That was... the person dearest to me.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Perhaps I should take my leave now. After all, my patrol isn't over yet.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Nod-Krai is a dangerous place to be at night. I'd advise that you head back soon as well.

choices.text: Or are you... also into moongazing?

talks.objective: Return to your accomodations to rest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ha... Went out to clear my head, and came back with even more on my mind...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(What on earth is {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} playing at...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hm? What's this...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon's Message
dialogues.text: "Paimon woke up and saw you were gone, so she made you a cup of berry juice to help you sleep... Her own secret recipe! When you get back, drink it up and go get yourself some rest."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Paimon's right... I need sleep. Got another full day of adventuring ahead...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Good... morning? If now still counts as morning, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When did you get back last night? Did you sleep well?

choices.text: Very well, thanks to your berry juice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, good to hear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So where'd you wander off to on your midnight stroll? Anything interesting to see in Nod-Krai at night?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: More than you'd believe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, really? C'mon, don't leave Paimon hanging!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright... Guess we'll have to feed your stomach before we feed Paimon's curiosity...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go grab something to eat while we talk!

choices.text: Rested up and ready to roll!

talks.objective: Go to The Flagship's main hall

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, this is just the best, huh? Free food, free lodgings... This Varka's friend-for-life material, that's for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: Hey, did you hear what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Ahvo
dialogues.text: Uh? Hear about what?

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: Y'know, all that commotion over at the Frostmoon Scions! Crazy, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ahvo
dialogues.text: Huh? ...Wh—What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: Pffft, see what I mean? Completely oblivious to what's going on around you!

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: The sacred relic of theirs... It's been stolen!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...! ... *cough* *cough*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, slow down! Paimon knows you're hungry, but you don't have to worry about her stealing your food... at least not today...

dialogues.speaker: Ahvo
dialogues.text: What!? Was it those Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: No idea, but the news has already spread right through Nasha Town!

dialogues.speaker: Ahvo
dialogues.text: What did their high priestess... Uhhh, what do they call her again, the Moon-something... Anyway, what did she say about it?

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: What COULD she say? She's the one who discovered it was missing!

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: She was in Nasha Town first thing this morning, hoping to launch a joint investigation with the Voynich Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whoa, did you hear that, {NICKNAME}? Lauma and the others... their sacred relic's been stolen!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who in Tevyat would even have the nerve—!? Paimon bets it was that bunch of good-for-nothing, rule-breaking, trouble-makin' Fatui!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(But {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} and I were the only ones to enter the secret chamber last night... Could it have been {M#her}{F#him}?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong? You feeling okay?

dialogues.speaker: Ahvo
dialogues.text: Hahaha... A joint investigation? Pff, good luck getting any takers — unless there's some reward or business opportunity to sweeten the deal.

dialogues.speaker: Jolanta
dialogues.text: Same thoughts here. So, just a few minutes back, she switched gears and headed over to the one place that might actually be able to solve this... the Curatorium of Secrets!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wah! Y—You scared Paimon... What is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh... O—Okay, just— Hey, Paimon's not a baby, y'know! Quit pulling her arm!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After Jahoda is finally brought up to speed, you all agree on a plan to infiltrate the Fatui research facility the following night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we sure Jahoda's alright? She looked totally crushed just now...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: She'll be fine, she's just in shock. But one thing's for sure — the Curatorium's professional standards are beyond question.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The fact that she only requested one day to prepare says it all.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As an apology, I'll ask my animal friends to help her out more often in the future...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Also... Thank you for being honest with me, {NICKNAME}. It means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was my fault in the first place...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Was it really, though?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As far as I see it, trusting your family is never "wrong." In this case, let's call it... a misjudgment.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But the truth is, we all make mistakes every now and then. What matters is how we deal with the consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So... In return for your sincerity, there's something I'd like to share with the two of you as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Perhaps it is something best said under the moon's gentle light. Would the two of you meet me on Hiisi Island tonight?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No problem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, it does sound important... You're right, there's too many people here. Somewhere quieter makes a lot more sense.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you both for understanding. Then let us meet beneath the moonlight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lauma, we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Lauma, are you... praying?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I am indeed... For the moment I was born, my people exclaimed: "Behold: eyes like the moonlit tide, antlers like the crescent moon, and blood that glimmers silver as the moon's reflection..."

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: From as far back as I can remember, I was revered as the "Frostmoon's Emissary" and the "Moon-Tide Maiden"...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The first words I ever learned were prayers to the Frostmoon... the first gestures, those of our sacred rites.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that... must have been tough.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Back then, I didn't know any better. It all just seemed so... natural.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The Frostmoon Scions' bloodline has long since begun to run thin. Nowadays, even those of us with antlers are few and far between, let alone those attuned to the power of kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But I...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Your antlers are so pretty...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They say it's an extraordinarily rare condition... once in a century, if that. I am unusually sensitive to the moonlight, as well as to the kuuvahki's ebb and flow. As a child, I could barely sleep because of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... It was that serious?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: To others, fluctuations in kuuvahki are something you easily get used to — like a gentle tide lapping away at the shore.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But to me, that same tide is a towering tsunami, a surging swell crashing against me...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Of course, as the years went by, I learned how to suppress my senses — and my power — enough to keep it all from overwhelming me.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But because of that... I also had to walk the path of concealment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Concealment...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: From the moment I was first taught to pray, my kin would point up to the night sky, telling me: "That, Lauma, is the Frostmoon — the last of the moons, the sole surviving truth."

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But I would ask them in response: "Why? Why can't I feel anything from it at all?"

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Later, I came to understand that they simply could not tell where the real tide was coming from. They couldn't sense it... the true moon beyond the sky's veil.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is Lauma talking about the false sky? So the true Frost Moon... lies beyond it?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: "The moon is false"... I reached that conclusion long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But there was no one I could tell, not a single soul... At least, not until now.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: "Am I the one who's wrong? Is it the moon that is false, or my own senses?" ...I asked myself such questions, time and time again.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #Thank you... {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: When you called yourself a Descender, I had a feeling you might be able to confirm what I had always suspected.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: And now that you have, it's exactly as I imagined. I feel... relieved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, Paimon kinda gets why you couldn't tell anyone now... It's not easy to change people's minds on something they've believed for hundreds of years.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That's what I meant by "concealment"...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I knew too much, so I had no choice but to keep my people in the dark... Every prayer I offer feels like a lie to keep myself going.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So that's what she meant when she asked me that question...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ("If you were aware of something, a secret that could hurt your family... Would you be honest with them, or try to hide it?")

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #{NICKNAME}... You've already met our "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar", haven't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? When was that, and more importantly, when were you planning on telling Paimon!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That night when I went out walking alone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, no wonder...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What did you think of her?

choices.text: A little... up in the clouds?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What exactly do you mean by "up in the clouds"...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I understand what you mean. She is quite indifferent to the world outside herself. But... I find it hard to hold that against her.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Yes. It was shortly after the fall of the Ancient Moon's Remnants.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I asked her what the Frostmoon Scions meant to her, and why she left in the first place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so, why did she...?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Perhaps... it's better if you ask her yourselves. Things tend to get lost in translation when you speak on someone's behalf.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What I can say for certain is this. Even when I had no one to confide in, I still had a family... I still had the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But that girl, born beneath the moonlight... perhaps she's never felt she had either.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The truth is, though, she might have had it all — if only the Frostmoon Scions hadn't let her down.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Last time I saw her, she kept looking up at the sky... Was she staring at the real moon beyond the false firmament?)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The Frostmoon Scions now walk a path of error. They offer their prayers to a false moon, and to a goddess who can no longer answer them.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I want to change all that.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But with the Fatui closing in on us day by day, the Frostmoon Scions must stand united — now more than ever. I just... need to wait for the right moment.

response.speaker: Kapy
response.text: Lady Lauma, Lady Lauma!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Kapy...? Has Kaarina's condition deteriorated again?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we'll have to continue this conversation later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait up, we'll come too!

choices.text: The sky above Teyvat... is a lie.

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Why...? Did I do something wrong? I've been praying to the Moon Goddess every day... Why isn't she getting any better...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Moon Goddess is powerless to answer her prayers, just like Lauma said...)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Kapy, I need you to wait outside. I'm about to start her treatment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can do to help...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Just... don't be alarmed by what you're about to see. And please, don't let her mother see it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is that... a knife!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Silver blood, and... medicine powder?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Shh... Please... Help me keep this a secret...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She looks much better now... But Lauma, was that...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...A medicine prescribed by a local doctor. For ordinary people, my blood has the power to counteract any adverse reactions to kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lauma's hands are covered in scars... Has she been secretly treating people like this all along...?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: *sigh* So now you know another of my little secrets...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I had hoped to guide the Scions out of error before Kaarina's illness reached this stage. But clearly... I was too late.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Changing old beliefs is never easy... Some are simply too deeply ingrained, just like this girl's mother's...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: My life... is as hidden from sight as the far side of the moon. Yet people only look to the bright side for guidance.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If the day ever came when the two sides were reversed... could they truly accept it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(Why am I thinking of {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} right now...? Has {M#she}{F#he} been forced to keep a part of {M#her}{F#his} life hidden too?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(If it was {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hearing you say that... puts my heart at ease.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm! And if there's anything we can do to help the Frostmoon Scions, just let us know!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Our priority right now is reclaiming our relic from the Fatui.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But I now understand... that the day I will tell everyone the truth is no longer far off.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Remind me... Who are you again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She forgot me after a single day...?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...A different one floats by your side today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ("A different one"!? What's that even supposed to mean? Ugh, there goes Paimon's perfect conversation starter...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh, h—hi there... Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, there you are. Hmm. Between the two, I suppose you're cuter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Wait, what does she mean Paimon's less cute than that... floaty thing!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's your favorite kind of food?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Is this... a treat? Or... an offering?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uhh, let's go with "treat"! Anyway, this is all {NICKNAME}'s cooking — so please, help yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (That wasn't exactly a "yes," but she didn't turn it down either. What could she be thinking?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Now you see what I've been dealing with...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: So... What do you want to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Hey, she's actually playing along... Quick, now's our shot!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know the moon in the sky isn't real, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I know there is only one moon in the sky. It is simply that some can see it... and some cannot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What does it mean to you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The missing prologue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (What does that mean? Isn't she going to explain herself?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you tell me more about that melody? You were humming it last time, too. It must be important to you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It is all I remember from the moment of my birth — a melody, a few lines of lyrics, like a lullaby from a foggy dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So, who was singing it?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I do not know.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I have nothing else. Just that song.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And the Frostmoon Scions who found me... they had nothing either, but hope.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Before I even knew what was happening, they were already calling me their "Goddess." And I... had no reason to decline.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Like two lost infants unknowingly exchanged, I adopted their faith, and in return, they adopted me.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But my adoption drops you into the story halfway through. What came before was scribbled onto the wrong pages... never even bound into the book.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That sense of something missing only served to nurture their greed and doubt. And thus, I came to realize that this place was never truly my home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greed and doubt?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: "O Moon Goddess, forge weapons for us, drive out our enemies, and expand our lands..."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: "O Moon Goddess, heal our wounds, ease our suffering, grant us strength..."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They asked for everything, and I obliged... until the day came when no answer could be given.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If mortals can turn to the gods when they are powerless... then who do the gods turn to when they have nothing left to give?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, you've... got Paimon there...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: In those days, the Frostmoon Scions cared more for "faith" than for "truth."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So that's why she chose to leave...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Reality rewrote the sky in words I could not understand. I did not want to read a tampered version, so I simply stopped looking.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The real beginning of my story lies up there on the moon, forever beyond my reach — like a message carved for blind hands, sealed away where no fingers can find it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's how it is...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mph...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The flowers... they've turned white?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: *pant*... You should go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What, now? But, you really don't look well... Did something just happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No... Aside from answers, I have nothing else to give you in return.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: This is the price... of running away from home a second time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Running away from home...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh... Is she heading towards the food? Did all of Paimon's questions make her hungry...?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you still have many questions?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I know I should offer more in return for your kindness, but I'm feeling a little worn out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, we're... so sorry about that!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Tsaritsa was right. Freedom always comes with a price.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: She said I could treat the Fatui as a second family, a second home... but in the end, they were no different. All they wanted in truth was my "power" as the Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I'd rather not dwell on such unhappy memories.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seems the Fatui can't afford to let go of such a valuable chess piece — so now they're coming for the Moon Goddess, their "Damselette in distress"...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I have fulfilled my promise to the Tsaritsa, though it has used up much of my power. So you see... this has nothing to do with betrayal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... you're just staying here for now, resting and recovering your strength?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about these flowers...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They have grown in Nod-Krai for many generations. They're highly sensitive to the ebb and flow of kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Kuuvahki...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So... they turn white when she's feeling weak. And when they went red that day, that was because... she was drawing upon her strength?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: At times, I thought about using that relic the Frostmoon Scions had hidden away. I could sense the power within it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But going out is such a hassle... People might see me, and I promised Lauma I wouldn't show myself to anyone. Besides, I know it's gone now anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Lauma asked you to stay in hiding...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh-oh, she's looking back at the food again!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Paimon's still got some little krumkakes here! You could have these for dessert if you wanted...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Lauma said she wishes to "change" the Frostmoon Scions... Which is why she asked me to stay out of sight.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I don't really understand what she meant — and to be honest, it's not something that concerns me. But I wasn't planning to see anyone, anyway. If they found their way here themselves, that's hardly my fault.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If The Damselette appeared in front of them now, the Frostmoon Scions might very well think that their Lady Kuutar has returned to save them...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (When you look at it that way, I guess Lauma's actions do make sense.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Lauma, the Maiden of the Grove... She is quite unlike any Frostmoon Scion I've ever met before.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: After hearing my story, she actually apologized for how the Frostmoon Scions treated me back then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She told us she feels like she's been living on the far side of the moon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is that so? I actually got the opposite impression...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: She's been keeping her true power hidden away, afraid that people might be dazzled by its brilliance... and that they'd no longer be willing to look her way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Just like Kuutar back then... Maybe her light was simply too bright for anyone to see her as family?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what do you wish for now?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I wish to return to the moon... to the home where my story is written.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Right now... that is all I wish for.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And with that, The Damselette looks up to the sky and falls silent.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon return to The Flagship, reflecting on everything that's happened as you prepare for tomorrow's mission...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's give them some space so they can rest...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The singing's getting closer... but it sounds... a little melancholy...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? There's nothing here...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(Am I too far away? Can't {M#she}{F#he} hear me?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #...{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Even the sound of your footsteps takes me right back...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: #As a warrior, as a traveler... as my {M#big brother}{F#little sister}...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: We make a pretty great team, huh? Just like the old days.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: From what I understand, the path ahead is likely to be full of trials and challenges.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: A deterrence against intruders, and a test for those who truly seek entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I doubt the two of us will have any problems.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Let's keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The door's open...

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Come. We must be close.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Stay on your toes, now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you considered that I might be the more experienced between us?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's about time, and the moon's already up. Let's head over to the place we agreed to meet Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Mm, I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Still... If we get separated, things could get tricky. Best we move together and watch each other's backs.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Looks like this is the first trial.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Eh? A secret door?)
